findings.finding: RealReal beat the TOP of its own guide on all three lines in both 2026 quarters. Q2: GMV $617M vs $590-600M guided, revenue $192.6M vs $186-189M, adj. EBITDA $13.5M vs $11-12M. Q1: GMV $606M vs $585-600M, revenue $189.7M vs $185-189M, adj. EBITDA $13.1M vs $11-13M. The Q3 guide (GMV $610-620M, +17-19% y/y vs $520M in Q3'25) assumes GMV slows from 22-24% growth, which it has held for four straight quarters. Repeating the pattern gives revenue of roughly $200-202M, about +2% over the $196.7-196.9M consensus, which sits at the guide midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats above the guide were sold in 2026: Q1 (2026-05-07) -17.26% close-to-close despite the revenue beat and a FY raise, with a 220bp take-rate drop cited; Q2 (2026-08-06) -3.68% despite beats on every line and a raise. In 2025 they were bought: Q3'25 +38.09%, Q2'25 +16.15%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue ($196.7-196.9M) sits at the guide midpoint, not at the top of the guide where the company has landed twice this year. A beat of this pattern is the base case for anyone who reads the history, so it is largely expected. Part of the +29% 20-day run-up is probably this trade. If the market had fully priced a beat, consensus would sit above $198M.
findings.independence: Q1 actuals vs guide come from a separate document (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1832046/realreal-q1-earnings-call-highlights and Q4'25 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1573221/000157322126000009/real-20260226xex991pressre.htm for the Q1 guide). Shares the 'company guides conservatively' logic with the guidance finding below, but this one is about the reported quarter.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide (revenue $788-797M, GMV $2.535-2.565B) implies Q4 revenue of about $210-219M (+8-13% vs Q4'25 $194M) and Q4 GMV of $697-727M (+13-18% vs $616M), using H1 revenue $382.3M, H1 GMV $1,223M and Q3 at the guide midpoint. Both are well below the 17-19% revenue and 22-24% GMV growth of the last four quarters. The company has raised its FY guide at every 2026 print (revenue $765-780M to $770-784M to $788-797M), so another raise is the likely outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY raises came with both 2026 prints, and the stock fell on both (-17.26%, -3.68%). The 2025 raises (Q2'25, Q3'25) were bought, +16% and +38%.
findings.why_not_priced: Benzinga's Q4 consensus of $216.2M revenue already sits in the upper half of the implied range, so the street partly expects a raise. A raise beyond ~$800M FY would be new. The arithmetic deceleration in the guide is visible to anyone who does it. If the market were sure of a large raise, the skew would not be paying for downside.
findings.independence: Same company release as the reported-quarter finding, but it rests on a different fact: the implied Q4 deceleration, not the Q3 pattern. FY guide history comes from separate releases: Q4'25 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1573221/000157322126000009/real-20260226xex991pressre.htm) and Q1'26 (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1832046/realreal-q1-earnings-call-highlights).

findings.finding: The stock went into the print up 28.9% over 20 days and 10.1% over 5 days, from $8.90 on 2026-10-02 to $11.54, roughly back to its $11.79 June 30 level, which was the level before the -3.7% Q2 reaction. Options carry +5.25 vol points of put skew. The bar for a positive reaction has risen.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both 2026 prints were sold after beats. The baseline shows 2 up of 8 reactions with a 16.7% median absolute move, so this name punishes a crowded long setup.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up itself is in the price. The claim is that it raises the reaction bar, and the skew already says the same, so this agrees with the market's own lean and is partly priced. Short interest of 14.8% of float with 5.8 days to cover is a squeeze cushion that limits it.
findings.independence: The October price path is from AAII ($8.90 on 2026-10-02, https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/545822-why-the-realreal-inc8217s-real-stock-is-down-621); the June 30 $11.79 is the 10-Q warrant valuation input; run-up and skew are from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-15 the company refinanced its 13% all-in PIK/cash 2029 secured notes (~$147M) with a $150M Fortress term loan at SOFR+575 plus a $25M undrawn revolver, both maturing 2033. The deal saves about $4M of interest a year, ends PIK, and removes the December 2027 springing maturity. Management set a medium-term target to cut total debt to $150M: repay the $48.2M 2028 converts in cash, or have the $190.1M 2031 converts convert. The call will be the first chance to quantify the path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior earnings reaction on a refinancing. The stock went from about $8.90 (Oct 2) to $10.40 (Oct 19) around the announcement, so most of it has already been paid.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is a public 8-K and the stock has rallied since. The only new part is any Q4 interest-savings or leverage detail on the call. The answer to the financing question is that the money buys a cheaper refinancing and a longer maturity, not distress, so the sign is positive and small.
findings.independence: Debt amounts are corroborated by the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001573221/000157322126000053/real-20260630.htm): 2028 converts $48.2M, 2031 converts $190.1M, 2029 notes $146.9M.

findings.finding: There are 7.16M liability-classified warrants at a $1.71 strike, marked by Black-Scholes. The liability was $74.7M at a $11.79 share price on June 30. The stock was about $9.83 on Sep 14 and $8.90 on Oct 2, which implies a non-cash Q3 gain of roughly $15-20M. That likely puts GAAP net income positive, against GAAP EPS bars that run from -$0.08 to $0.00. This reverses the $18.6M Q2 charge that pushed GAAP to -$0.23.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Warrant swings have been large ($44M Q3'25 charge, $39M Q4'25 charge, $18.6M Q2'26 charge), and the stock moved on the operating lines in each case. No reaction is attributable to this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Headline-scraping algorithms compare GAAP EPS against a disputed consensus, so a positive GAAP EPS could print as a 'beat' in after-hours headlines. It has no path to guidance or the multiple, so it is sized as a fraction of the same money as operating profit. The EPS bar is disputed, so the size is capped.
findings.independence: The Sep 14 price of $9.83 is from Stock Titan (search snippet, https://www.stocktitan.net/news/REAL/) and the Oct 2 price of $8.90 from AAII. The exact Sep 30 close is unsourced.

findings.finding: Primary luxury peers reported US demand holding through Q3 2026, which matters for supply and demand at a US consignment marketplace. LVMH US organic revenue was +5% in Q3 (+6% in Q2), even as Fashion & Leather Goods fell 5% organically on China (reported 2026-10-12). Kering (2026-10-22) said North America was Gucci's most resilient market and group North America grew 2%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of REAL reacting to peer luxury prints at its own earnings. REAL's growth has decoupled from primary luxury: GMV grew 22% while LVMH fashion was flat to negative.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy. The weak read for REAL's supply would be a US luxury slowdown (consignors trading in less), and neither peer shows one. These peers spoke after REAL last did (Aug 6), but the readthrough is indirect and widely seen.
findings.independence: Kering Q3 2026, a different company and document: https://fashionunited.uk/news/business/kering-q3-revenue-remains-stable-as-jewelry-and-eyewear-offset-gucci-contraction/2026102391016

findings.finding: Morgan Stanley/WatchCharts estimate certified pre-owned Rolex sales at $229M in Q3 2026, +61% y/y and +30% q/q, so luxury watch resale demand was strong in the quarter. Watches and jewelry are a high-AOV category for REAL; it cited a $2.5M F.P. Journe consignment in Q2. But WatchCharts' September index showed Rolex resale prices -0.4%, so pricing was flat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history; AOV +13% in Q2 has been partly a mix shift to high-value items, which also compressed the take rate.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (Q3 2026 estimate; date in article, URL carries no year)
findings.why_not_priced: Industry proxy, not company-confirmed. It is sized small, and the transmission to REAL's GMV is unconfirmed by the company.
findings.independence: WatchCharts September 2026 index (https://watchcharts.com/articles/p/9508) shows flat-to-down prices, which partly cuts against this, so the size stays small.

findings.finding: Take-rate compression continues inside the Q3 guide. Revenue/GMV at the guide midpoint is 31.9% ($196M/$615M) against 33.5% in Q3'25 ($174M/$520M), and revenue growth (+11.5-13.8% guided) is running well below GMV growth (+17-19%). The Q1 take-rate drop of 220bp to 36.4% was the cited cause of the -17% Q1 reaction. If the high-AOV mix shift deepens, revenue can miss even on a GMV beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: take rate -220bp and the stock -17.26% despite the revenue beat (Seeking Alpha headline 'sinks despite Q1 revenue beat and 24% GMV growth').
findings.why_not_priced: The compression is inside what the company guided, so it is expected. The risk is that it runs worse than guided. This finding lands inside the guide and is sized small for that reason.

outside_window.finding: ThredUp reports Q3 2026 on 2026-11-04 after the close. Its weak Q3 guide (revenue $87-89M, +7%) drew a ~30% drop after Q2. It is a peer readthrough, but it lands after REAL's exit window.

The refinancing's Q4 loss on extinguishment of the 2029 notes (redeemed at par about Oct 19, with ~$2.6M carrying discount at June 30) lands in Q4 reporting, not this window, apart from any call mention.

baseline_tension: The findings cut both ways. The fundamental read (beat above guide plus a likely FY raise) leans against the skew. The run-up, 2026's sell-the-beat history and the take-rate risk agree with the skew. Net it agrees mildly with the skew, offset by a 14.8%-of-float short as a squeeze cushion.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): both 2026 beat-and-raise prints were sold, so the reported-quarter beat goes +1.0 to +0.5 and the FY-raise guidance finding +1.0 to +0.6; p_up 51 to 49.
Lesson 6 (the bar): the revenue bar is sourced to two agreeing estimates plus the guide, so it stands. The EPS bar is disputed, so the GAAP warrant one-off is cut +0.3 to +0.2.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest of 14.8% of float with 5.8 days to cover is a moderate squeeze cushion, so the run-up/skew positioning negative is trimmed -2.0 to -1.8.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the refinancing buys a cheaper, longer maturity and is not distress, so it stays a small positive at +0.3.
Lessons 2 and 5 (one-offs and proxies): the warrant one-off and the peer/watch proxies were already sized small and are left standing.
